Let’s talk about something that really shapes our relationship with money—self-awareness.
Think about it: Money isn’t just about numbers or budgets. It’s personal. Our beliefs, habits, and emotions all play a role, and most of the time, we don’t even notice how much they’re driving us.
So many of us go through life on autopilot, repeating patterns we picked up as kids or just soaking up the attitudes of the people around us. But real progress? That starts when you’re willing to look inward and ask, “Why do I make the choices I do?”
Let me share a quick story. There was a woman who always felt anxious when it came to spending, even though she had enough money. She started digging into those feelings and realized they went all the way back to her parents, who struggled financially and stressed over every purchase. Once she understood where that anxiety came from, she could finally make choices that balanced both caution and enjoyment—without guilt.
And here’s something to pay attention to: Most of us don’t realize how much our money habits are shaped by what you might call “invisible scripts.” Maybe you spend to feel loved, or you save just to feel safe. Some people try not to think about money at all, hoping any problems will just disappear.
But the more you get to know your own motivations, the easier it becomes to make choices that actually serve you—choices you can feel good about.
Now, self-awareness isn’t about judging yourself, or blaming your past. It’s about curiosity. It’s asking, “Why do I do this?” and, “Is it helping or hurting me?” Sure, it can feel a little uncomfortable at first, but it’s also incredibly freeing. The more you understand, the more you’re in control.
Over time, self-awareness changes everything about the way you approach money. You become less reactive, more intentional, and you start to align your choices with your real values.
The journey isn’t always easy, but here’s the key takeaway: self-awareness is the foundation for real, lasting change.
